issues.legal_issue: Formulating a scheme to comply with a judgment while an appeal is pending does not, by itself, prevent the government from challenging that judgment.
material_facts: After the writ judgment, the government formulated a scheme extending equivalent training to the excluded trainees while contempt proceedings were pending.
The government had already filed its challenge to the writ judgment, and the appellate court later stayed the judgment.
issues.conclusion: The formulation of the scheme during the interval before the appeal was first listed did not debar the government from questioning the correctness of the writ judgment.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the circumstances in which the scheme was formulated—including its timing amid contempt proceedings and the subsequent stay of the judgment—meant that its mere formulation did not prevent the government from pursuing its appeal.

predicates.government_appeal_from_writ_judgment: The government appealed a judgment directing it to extend a benefit to a group of trainees.
predicates.scheme_formulated_after_judgment_during_: The government formulated a scheme extending that benefit after the judgment while the challenge to the judgment was pending.

issues.definition: When the government appeals a writ judgment and formulates a scheme extending the disputed benefit while its challenge is pending, that formulation does not by itself bar the appeal.

issues.legal_issue: A government may reserve additional training for one group under an employment-related policy when the groups are meaningfully distinct and the classification has a rational connection to the policy's objective.
material_facts: The government provided additional training as veterinary pharmacists only to trainees from a scheme designed to train unemployed residents to provide basic veterinary services in their panchayats.
Those trainees had been selected by a committee, had received training directed at veterinary treatment and breeding, and were intended to work as self-employed service providers.
The opening of veterinary dispensaries had limited the trainees’ opportunity to work independently, and the government assessed a need for veterinary pharmacists in those dispensaries.

The other trainees came from a dairy scheme for small landholders, were not selected through a competitive process, and received training focused on cattle rearing and fodder production to establish dairy farms.
The dairy-scheme trainees had undertaken to pursue cattle rearing, and veterinary-pharmacist training was not necessary to fulfil the dairy scheme’s objectives.
The trainees challenging the policy did not establish hostile discrimination.
issues.conclusion: The distinction between the two groups was permissible, the government’s policy was not shown to be arbitrary or discriminatory, and the High Court’s direction was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 14 of the Constitution, a classification must rest on an intelligible differentia that distinguishes the groups and must have a rational relation to the objective sought. Courts generally do not interfere with executive policy unless it is demonstrably capricious or arbitrary, wholly without reason, discriminatory, or contrary to a statute or the Constitution. The Court applied these principles to the different eligibility criteria, selection processes, training, post-training assistance, and objectives of the two schemes.

rule.if: challenge_to_executive_training_policy and distinct_scheme_objectives and distinct_training_and_selection and rational_employment_response and not hostile_discrimination_established

predicates.challenge_to_executive_training_policy: Trainees challenged an executive policy that reserved additional training for one group.
predicates.distinct_scheme_objectives: The two groups were trained under schemes with different stated purposes.
predicates.distinct_training_and_selection: The groups differed in how their members were selected and in the focus of their training.
predicates.rational_employment_response: The government provided additional training to address the preferred group’s reduced opportunity for self-employment and a need for workers in public service facilities.
predicates.hostile_discrimination_established: The challenging trainees established that the government had treated their group with hostile discrimination.

issues.definition: When trainees challenge an executive training policy, the groups have different purposes and training arrangements, the policy responds rationally to an employment need, and hostile discrimination is not established, reserving the additional training for one group is permissible.
